chunks: My father (rah) said: It was narrated to me by Ali ibn Musa from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from Ali ibn al-Hakam from Hashim ibn Safwan from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:
One who comes to know of a reward for a good deed and performs it, he will have that reward, even if the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him) did not say it.
ai.seo_question: Does performing a good deed with a known reward grant the reward even if the Prophet did not explicitly mention it?
ai.summary: Shaykh al-Saduq uses this narration to establish the principle of *istishab* (presumption of continuity) in rewards, affirming that the merit of a deed is not limited to the Prophet's explicit verbal endorsement but extends to any good act performed with the intention of seeking divine reward. This underscores the Shia scholarly view that the spiritual efficacy of an action is rooted in the act itself and the believer's intent, rather than solely in specific prophetic formulas.
